name: Adobe Firefly
levelNote: A single image is easy to try; a full campaign means managing models, reference frames and credits.
what: Adobe's generative suite for images, vectors, video and audio, with Adobe and partner models, built to hand off into Creative Cloud apps.
anchor: Like image generation in ChatGPT or Gemini, but the output drops straight into Photoshop, Illustrator and Premiere for real production work.
firstTask: Generate one product still from a reference image before trying video.
skip: You only need a few concept images. ChatGPT or Gemini will do that inside a plan you already pay for.

price.detail: US list prices: Firefly Free has limited daily generations. Standard US$9.99/mo (2,000 credits). Pro regularly US$19.99/mo (4,000). Pro Plus regularly US$49.99/mo (10,000). Introductory discounts were running when checked.

example.text: Adobe says retailer Currys used Composition Reference and Generative Expand on a campaign.

name: Runway
levelNote: A usable clip takes practice with reference images, motion prompts and retries.
what: A multi-model platform for generating and editing video, animating stills, and chaining steps into reusable workflows.
anchor: Like video generation in Gemini or ChatGPT, but with an editor, several video models side by side, and workflows you can reuse.
firstTask: Animate a single still with one camera move.
skip: You need one short clip. Try the video feature already in your assistant subscription first.

price.line: 125 one-time free credits · Standard US$12/mo billed yearly
price.detail: Free: 125 credits once, not monthly. Standard US$12/mo billed yearly (625 credits a month). Pro US$28/mo billed yearly (2,250). Max US$76/mo billed yearly (9,500). A first-year discount was running when checked.

example.text: Runway says Studio Unveil used its Gen-4.5 and Aleph models in a hybrid live-action and AI campaign for Salomon.

name: Higgsfield
levelNote: Presets help, but choosing a model and directing camera motion takes practice. The MCP connection is a separate, more technical path.
what: A multi-model image and video platform with Cinema Studio for camera direction and studios for ads and short videos.
anchor: Like asking Gemini or ChatGPT for a video, but you direct the camera move and lens look instead of hoping the prompt lands.
firstTask: Try one slow push-in on a product photo you own.
skip: Your current video model already makes a usable shot. Use your assistant for scripts and shot lists instead.

price.detail: Free plan: 0 monthly credits, selected models only. Starter US$19/mo (270 credits). Plus list price US$59/mo (1,200 credits). A Black Friday sale ending Nov 29, 2026 was running when checked.

example.text: Higgsfield says olive-oil brand Alya Health used Claude with Higgsfield's MCP connection to make video ads.

name: Canva (and Canva MCP)
levelNote: Templates and editable text give you a starting point with no setup. The MCP connection for AI assistants is a developer step.
what: A template-first design platform. Its MCP server, generally available since Nov 2026, lets Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and other assistants create editable Canva designs.
anchor: Like asking Claude or ChatGPT to make a flyer, but you get a real, editable, on-brand Canva design instead of a flat image.
firstTask: Edit one promo template with your own photo and offer text, then resize it for a second format.
skip: You only need the copy or a rough layout. Your assistant can draft that without a new tool.

price.detail: US prices: Free US$0 with limited AI. Pro US$18/mo. Business US$25/mo per person. A 50% promotion was showing when checked. Canva MCP: sign up in the Canva Developer Portal.

claims.text: Canva says nearly 500,000 people signed up through its MCP in the month before general availability.

name: Photoroom
levelNote: Start with one upload and a guided edit. Batch work and the API are optional.
what: An AI product-photo editor for background removal, product scenes, catalog batches and short product videos from photos you already have.
anchor: Like asking ChatGPT to clean up a product photo, but built for doing 200 listing photos the same way, with real edges and shadows.
firstTask: Remove the background from one product photo and check the edges.
skip: You need one mockup. Try ChatGPT or Gemini, and use real photos whenever product accuracy matters.

price.detail: Pro US$7.50/mo billed yearly (8,000 AI credits, 1,000 exports). Max US$20.99/mo billed yearly. Ultra US$82.50/mo billed yearly. Monthly billing costs more.

example.text: Photoroom says print-on-demand company Completeful used its API to automate product mockups.

name: Hermes Agent
levelNote: Expect to configure model providers and tools, manage file access and decide what the agent may do.
what: Nous Research's open-source (MIT license) agent that you run on your own machine or server, connecting models, tools and files for repeatable tasks.
anchor: Like Projects in Claude or custom GPTs in ChatGPT, but it runs on your own computer, on any model, and keeps working on a schedule.
firstTask: Have it turn a short brief into a local checklist before you give it wider permissions.
skip: You need a draft or a one-off task. Your chat assistant is simpler and has no setup.

price.line: Free to self-host · hosted Plus US$20/mo
price.detail: The agent is free and open source. Model and hosting costs depend on what you connect. Nous Portal hosted plans start at Plus US$20/mo.

source.label: Hermes Agent: open source and hosted

disclosure: Used to build this directory. The first draft of this page was prepared with Hermes Agent, so we list it but do not rank it.
status: Researched · used to build this directory

name: Wispr Flow
levelNote: Install, hold a key, talk. It works in any app.
what: A dictation app for Mac, Windows, iPhone and Android that turns speech into clean text in any app, plus a meeting notetaker.
anchor: Like voice mode in ChatGPT or Gemini, but it types what you say into any app on your computer, not just the chat box.
firstTask: Dictate one email reply and compare it with what you would have typed.
skip: Your phone's built-in dictation already gets your words right.

price.detail: Free US$0 on Mac, Windows, iPhone and Android. Pro US$15/user/mo monthly or US$12 billed yearly. Growth and Enterprise add admin controls.

claims.text: Wispr says its Canto-2 model cut average transcription error across 14 languages from 9.9% to 6.3% in its own internal benchmark (report in Chinese).

name: Obsidian Skills
levelNote: You need a coding agent (such as Claude Code or Codex) and an Obsidian vault.
what: Official agent skills that teach AI agents to read and write Obsidian notes and its open formats: Markdown, Bases and JSON Canvas.
anchor: Like Projects in Claude holding your files, but your notes stay as plain Markdown files on your own computer and the agent learns Obsidian's formats.
firstTask: Point your agent at one vault folder and ask it to build an index note.
skip: You don't keep notes in Obsidian, or you don't use a coding agent.

price.detail: Open source under the MIT license. Obsidian itself is free.

name: Perplexity Teammates
levelNote: Setup is guided, but you have to connect tools and describe the work it should own.
what: Long-running Perplexity agents that own ongoing work, such as watching competitors or chasing stalled sales conversations, and bring results back for review.
anchor: Like scheduled tasks in ChatGPT or Deep Research in Gemini, but each teammate keeps a standing job, remembers it, and can take requests in Slack.
firstTask: Create one teammate that watches three competitor pricing pages and reports weekly.
skip: You need one research answer, not an ongoing job. Deep research in your current assistant covers that.

price.detail: Launched on the web for Perplexity Max subscribers, iPhone app promised. Free and Pro users can upgrade in Settings. Max price is listed on Perplexity's pricing page.

name: Google AI Mode with Personal Intelligence
levelNote: It's Google Search. Connecting your apps is an opt-in setting.
what: AI Mode in Google Search can, if you opt in, connect to Google Drive, Google Wallet and the Gemini app to give answers based on your own stuff.
anchor: Like connecting Google Drive to ChatGPT or Claude, but inside the Google Search box you already use.
firstTask: Turn on one connection (Drive) and ask a question your own documents can answer.
skip: You'd rather not link your personal accounts to Search. It works without them.

price.line: Part of Google Search · no separate price stated
price.detail: Google's announcement does not list a price; it is opt-in and can be turned off.

name: Scientific Agent Skills
levelNote: For researchers using a coding agent; each skill brings its own tools and data sources.
what: A library of ready-made agent skills for scientific work, such as literature search, bioinformatics and chemistry tasks.
anchor: Like custom GPTs or Gems built for a lab, but they plug into coding agents such as Claude Code and run real analysis tools.
firstTask: Install it and ask your agent for a literature summary on one narrow question.
skip: You aren't doing hands-on research work. This is a researcher's toolkit.

price.detail: Open source under the MIT license; you pay for the AI model your agent uses.

claims.text: The maintainers say it is used by more than 250,000 scientists (self-reported).

name: Claude Ship
levelNote: For software teams on GitHub. You write the policy for what Claude may approve.
what: Claude reviews pull requests, fixes failing checks and merge conflicts (PR Steward), and approves changes your team's written policy allows (Claude Approvals).
anchor: Like asking Claude to review your code in a chat, but it sits on every GitHub pull request and can fix and approve within rules you set.
firstTask: Turn on Code Review in observe-only mode for one repository.
skip: You're a solo builder without a review process. A chat review is enough.

price.line: Claude Team and Enterprise · billed on tokens
price.detail: Available on Claude Team and Enterprise plans for GitHub repositories. Code Review is generally available; PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta. Usage is billed on tokens, and admins can set spend limits.

name: Claude artifacts as desktop apps
levelNote: Ask Claude for a small tool, then press Install as app. No coding or packaging.
what: Turn a small app Claude builds in a chat (an artifact) into a Mac or Windows app with its own icon and window. It can use your connectors and, with permission, send notifications.
anchor: Like Canvas in ChatGPT or Gemini, but the thing you made becomes a real desktop app you open every day.
firstTask: Ask Claude for a one-screen tracker you'd use daily, then install it.
skip: You need a phone app, or your organization has turned the feature off.

price.line: Beta on all Claude plans · Pro US$20/mo
price.detail: Rolling out in beta on all plans in Claude for Mac and Windows; requests count toward your plan's usage limits. Claude Free is US$0; Pro is US$20/mo (US$17/mo billed yearly).

name: Spec Kit
levelNote: Comfortable with a terminal and a coding agent.
what: GitHub's open-source toolkit for spec-driven development: write what you want first, then let a coding agent plan and build from that spec.
anchor: Like asking Claude or ChatGPT to plan an app before coding it, but the plan becomes a living spec your coding agent keeps following.
firstTask: Write a one-page spec for a small tool and let your agent generate the plan.
skip: You're prototyping something throwaway. Just ask your assistant to build it.

price.detail: Open source under the MIT license; you pay for the AI model your agent uses.

name: text-to-cad
levelNote: You run it through a coding agent and should know basic CAD and 3D printing.
what: Free, open-source CAD for AI agents such as Codex and Claude Code: it generates STEP, STL and 3MF models, checks design for manufacturing, and makes drawings.
anchor: Like asking ChatGPT to describe a bracket, but you get a real 3D model file you can print or send to a machine shop.
firstTask: Ask for a simple wall bracket with exact dimensions and print it.
skip: You don't make physical parts. This is for makers and engineers.

price.detail: The project's site says it is 100% open source and free; MIT license on GitHub.

name: OpenCode
levelNote: Comfortable in a terminal or a code editor.
what: An open-source coding agent for the desktop, terminal or phone that works with free models or 200+ AI providers, including Claude, GPT and Gemini.
anchor: Like Claude Code or Codex, but open source and not tied to one model company.
firstTask: Use the free models to explain and tidy one small script.
skip: You already have Claude Code or Codex and like it.

price.line: Free models, no account · bring your own plan
price.detail: Comes with free models and needs no account; you can connect your own subscription or use OpenCode Go.

name: Open Code Review
levelNote: For developers who can run it in their own pipeline.
what: Alibaba's open-source code-review tool that combines fixed checks with an AI agent to leave precise, line-level review comments.
anchor: Like pasting a diff into Claude for review, but self-hosted, in your pipeline, and combining rule-based checks with the AI pass.
firstTask: Run it on one recent pull request and compare it with a human review.
skip: You're not running a code-review pipeline. A chat review is simpler.

price.detail: Open source under the Apache 2.0 license; you pay for the AI model it calls.

name: GLM-5.4 (Z.ai Coding Plan)
levelNote: You plug the model into a coding tool such as Claude Code, Cline or OpenCode.
what: Z.ai's coding subscription, now running GLM-5.4, a 750-billion-parameter model that loops 28 of its layers twice. Works inside existing coding tools.
anchor: Like paying for Claude or ChatGPT to power your coding agent, but a lower-cost model you swap in under the same tools.
firstTask: Point OpenCode or Cline at the plan and run one familiar task you've done with Claude.
skip: You need published, independent benchmarks before switching. Z.ai's comparison is its own claim.

price.detail: Z.ai's page says plans start from 18 a month; the currency is not shown in the text we read. GLM-5.4 API and open weights are promised later.

claims.text: Z.ai claims GLM-5.4 reaches intelligence comparable to 2-to-3-trillion-parameter models; it has not published full benchmark scores.

name: Chrome DevTools MCP
levelNote: For web developers using a coding agent.
what: Gives coding agents Chrome DevTools through MCP (Model Context Protocol) or a CLI, so they can open a real browser, check their work and run Lighthouse audits.
anchor: Like Claude in Chrome or ChatGPT's agent clicking around, but for developers: the agent inspects and tests the site it just built.
firstTask: Ask your agent to load your site and report the slowest part of the page.
skip: You don't build websites.

price.detail: Open source under the Apache 2.0 license.

name: Nod
levelNote: A desktop installer, then you connect your AI provider and apps.
what: An open-source personal agent with its own sandboxed computer and browser. It chases invoices, preps calls and cancels trials on real websites, and asks before it acts.
anchor: Like ChatGPT's agent mode, but it runs on your own machine, uses the AI provider you choose, and asks before every action.
firstTask: Give it one errand: check a pricing page every week and tell you when it changes.
skip: You don't want to manage API keys or an AI provider bill.

price.line: Free · you pay your AI provider
price.detail: Nod is open source (Apache 2.0) and free; you pay your model provider, or connect a model running on your own computer. Research preview.

claims.text: n8n says that in 678 test runs Nod took zero actions without permission (self-reported).

name: Gemini computer use for Mac
levelNote: Built into the Gemini Mac app; you choose which apps it may use.
what: Gemini can operate Mac apps and websites in a background window while you keep working, with a live preview in the chat.
anchor: Like Claude's or ChatGPT's computer use, but built into the Gemini app for Mac and running in the background.
firstTask: Ask it to collect three numbers from a website into a spreadsheet.
skip: You're outside the U.S., on Windows, or on a free Google account.

price.line: Google AI Plus, Pro or Ultra · U.S., English
price.detail: Requires an Apple silicon Mac on macOS 15 or later, a personal Google account (18+), and Google AI Plus, Pro or Ultra. Rolling out in English in the U.S.

name: Google Workspace MCP servers and CLI
levelNote: For developers and admins connecting agents to Workspace.
what: Google's official way for AI agents to use Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Chat and Tasks, with user confirmations, audit logs and admin controls.
anchor: Like connecting Gmail to Claude or ChatGPT, but Google's own governed connector that any agent can use.
firstTask: Connect a test account and let an agent summarize one Drive folder.
skip: You only use Gemini's built-in Workspace features. They already have access.

price.line: Standard tier at no cost, with quotas
price.detail: Standard tier: no cost with published usage quotas. Scaled tier: charges for usage above daily free allowances from April 1, 2027.

name: Eney
levelNote: An app you install; it asks before it sends, edits or moves anything.
what: A proactive assistant for Mac and iPhone that suggests next steps from what's on your screen, transcribes meetings without a bot, and drafts replies.
anchor: Like the ChatGPT desktop app, but it speaks up first with suggestions and works across your Mac's files and apps.
firstTask: Let it transcribe one meeting and draft the follow-up email.
skip: You're on Windows or Android, or you'd rather not have an assistant watching your screen.

price.detail: Free for 14 days with 10,000 AI credits, then Starter US$14.99/mo (10,000 credits) or Boost US$29.99/mo (25,000); higher tier available.

name: Anthropic Agent Skills
levelNote: Skills install into Claude or a coding agent; reading one is easy, writing your own takes practice.
what: Anthropic's public library of Agent Skills: folders of instructions and scripts that teach Claude and other agents repeatable tasks such as making documents and spreadsheets.
anchor: Like custom instructions in ChatGPT, but packaged per task, shareable, and loaded only when the task comes up.
firstTask: Add one document skill and ask Claude for a formatted report.
skip: You only chat casually. Skills pay off when you repeat the same task.

price.detail: Public repository; licenses vary by skill. Using skills counts toward your Claude plan or API usage.

name: ComfyUI
levelNote: Node-based workflows give full control but take real learning.
what: An open-source, node-based app for building image, video, 3D and audio generation workflows, on your own computer or in Comfy Cloud.
anchor: Like image generation in ChatGPT or Grok, but you wire every step yourself and run open models on your own machine.
firstTask: Load a ready-made workflow from the Comfy library and change one setting.
skip: You want quick images, not control. Your assistant is faster.

price.line: Free desktop app · Comfy Cloud optional
price.detail: The desktop app is open source (GPL-3.0) and free; Comfy Cloud and model-provider usage are paid options.

name: HyperFrames
levelNote: The Studio app needs no code; the agent-skill route uses Claude Code, Codex or Cursor.
what: HeyGen's free, open-source way to make videos with an AI agent: the agent writes each scene as HTML and HyperFrames renders it to video.
anchor: Like asking Claude or ChatGPT for a video script, but your agent actually builds and renders the video, scene by scene.
firstTask: Make a 20-second product teaser from your own website in the Studio app.
skip: You need filmed footage edited, not motion graphics.

price.line: Free, open source · Studio Pro US$25/mo
price.detail: Framework, CLI, agent skills and browser editor are free (Apache 2.0) with no watermark on local renders. HyperFrames Studio has a Free plan; Pro is US$25/mo with 25,000 credits.

name: Lottie AI
levelNote: Describe an animation in a sentence; refine with sliders.
what: Turns a one-sentence description into an editable vector animation (Lottie format) you can tweak and export for apps and websites.
anchor: Like asking ChatGPT for an image, but you get a lightweight, editable animation that plays on a website or in an app.
firstTask: Describe a loading animation in your brand colours and export it.
skip: You need video, not interface animation.

price.line: 10 free generations · paid plans add credits
price.detail: Starter (free) workspaces get 10 Lottie AI generations in total; they don't reset. Paid plans include a monthly AI credit balance.

name: Suno (with Visuals)
levelNote: Type an idea, get a song. Studio features go deeper.
what: An AI music maker. Its Visuals tab turns songs into short lip-synced video clips or cover art.
anchor: Like asking ChatGPT or Gemini for song lyrics, but you get the finished, sung track and a clip to go with it.
firstTask: Make a 30-second jingle for something you care about.
skip: You need music you can use commercially on the free plan. Commercial use needs a paid plan.

price.detail: Free US$0 with 50 song credits. Pro US$10/mo (US$8 billed yearly) with commercial use rights. Premier US$30/mo. Visuals are part of the top Platinum plan.

name: Cloudflare Search for Agents
levelNote: One switch in the Cloudflare dashboard, if your site already uses Cloudflare.
what: One toggle indexes your website and adds a search endpoint on your own domain, so AI agents can search your pages instead of crawling them one by one.
anchor: Like hoping ChatGPT or Gemini finds your business correctly, but you hand AI agents an official search of your own site.
firstTask: Switch it on for one site and ask an agent a question only your site answers.
skip: Your site isn't on Cloudflare.

price.detail: Available to all Cloudflare customers, including Free, with limits; usage counts toward your plan's included allowances.

name: DeepTutor
maker: University of Hong Kong Data Intelligence Lab
levelNote: You install it yourself (Python or Docker) and connect a model.
what: An open-source personal tutor: workspaces per subject, a notebook, study paths and practice, all driven by an AI agent you host.
anchor: Like Study mode in ChatGPT or Guided Learning in Gemini, but open source, self-hosted, and organized around your own materials.
firstTask: Make one workspace for a subject you're learning and add a single source.
skip: You want something that works in a browser tab today. Use your assistant's study mode.

price.detail: Open source under the Apache 2.0 license; you pay for the AI model you connect.

name: MuJoCo
levelNote: A research-grade physics simulator; the browser demos are easy, real use needs code.
what: Google DeepMind's open-source physics simulator, widely used to train and test robots in simulation before they touch real hardware.
anchor: Like asking Gemini how a robot arm works, but you can watch one move, fall and grip in a real physics simulation.
firstTask: Open the interactive browser showcase on mujoco.org and push a model around.
skip: You're not studying or building robots.

price.detail: Open source under the Apache 2.0 license.
